FIELD REFERENCE

Shoal bass (Micropterus cataractae): habitat and size

Shoal bass (Micropterus cataractae) are river bass native to the Apalachicola–Chattahoochee–Flint basin. They favor rocky shoals with moving water rather than still reservoir habitat. Alabama lists an adult size of 12–18 inches. Start your trip plan with the river reach, then check access and the current local rules.

Updated 2026-11-19 · Castward

Where do shoal bass live?

Key factDetail
Scientific nameMicropterus cataractae
Native basinApalachicola–Chattahoochee–Flint
HabitatRocky river shoals with moderate to fast current
Adult size12–18 inches, according to Outdoor Alabama
DietCrayfish, fish and insects

What should you know about shoal bass?

How big do shoal bass get?

Outdoor Alabama lists adults at 12–18 inches. The Florida Natural Areas Inventory describes fish up to 25 inches; that is not a typical catch size.

Are shoal bass the same as redeye bass?

No. Outdoor Alabama distinguishes them by tail-fin margins and tongue teeth. Shoal bass lack the white tail-fin margins and tongue teeth described for redeye bass.

Do shoal bass live in lakes?

Georgia DNR describes a river specialist that generally avoids reservoir habitat. Choose a river reach rather than assuming a nearby lake holds this fish.

What do shoal bass eat?

Georgia DNR lists crayfish, fish and insects. Diet changes with the size of the fish.

Does the native range show where I can fish today?

No. A native range is not a current access map. Check the named river reach and local rules before travel.
